Derek runs a small hardware and home goods store. Every few months, the same thing would happen — a supplier would sell out of something, he'd stay stocked up on it by accident because he checked inventory manually and didn't catch it fast enough, or worse, he'd run out of his best-sellers right before a busy weekend and scramble to reorder.

It wasn't a systems problem, exactly. It was a time problem. He was running a whole store by himself. Who has time to check every item's stock level every day?

Now, inventory alerts do that monitoring for him automatically. When anything drops below his set threshold, he gets a notification immediately — not when it's already too late, but right when he needs to act.
